subject: biology
topicDisplay: Theme A · Molecules & Cells (Water, Nucleic Acids, Cell Structure)
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other because water is:
questions.explain: Unequal sharing of electrons gives water partial charges, allowing hydrogen bonding.

questions.q: Attraction between water molecules themselves is called:
questions.explain: Cohesion (water-to-water) supports transport in xylem and surface tension.

questions.q: Water's high specific heat capacity means it:
questions.explain: Hydrogen bonding lets water absorb much heat with little temperature change, stabilising habitats.

questions.q: Sweating cools the body because water has a high:
questions.explain: Evaporating water removes large amounts of heat from the skin.

questions.q: Water is a good solvent for ions and polar molecules because:
options: Its polarity lets it surround charged particles
It forms covalent bonds with solutes
questions.explain: Polar water forms hydration shells around solutes, dissolving them.

questions.q: Glucose can be carried dissolved in blood plasma but lipids cannot because glucose is:
questions.explain: Polar, soluble glucose dissolves in plasma; nonpolar lipids need carrier proteins.

questions.q: A DNA nucleotide is composed of:
options: Deoxyribose, phosphate and a nitrogenous base
Ribose, phosphate and an amino acid
questions.explain: Each nucleotide has a sugar, a phosphate and one of four bases.

questions.q: In DNA, adenine pairs with:
questions.explain: A–T pair with two hydrogen bonds; G–C with three.

questions.q: The two strands of DNA are antiparallel, meaning they:
questions.explain: Antiparallel orientation is essential for replication and transcription.

questions.q: The sugar found in RNA is:
questions.explain: RNA contains ribose and uses uracil instead of thymine.

questions.q: If one DNA strand reads 5'-ATGC-3', its complementary strand is:
questions.explain: Complementary, antiparallel pairing gives T-A, A-T, C-G, G-C.

questions.q: The main role of DNA is to:
questions.explain: DNA's stable structure allows reliable storage and inheritance of genetic information.

questions.q: A key difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells is that eukaryotes have:
questions.explain: Eukaryotes compartmentalise functions; prokaryotes lack membrane-bound organelles.

questions.q: The organelle that carries out aerobic respiration is the:
questions.explain: Mitochondria produce most ATP via aerobic respiration.

questions.q: The rough endoplasmic reticulum functions in:
questions.explain: Ribosomes on the rough ER make proteins that are then processed and transported.

questions.q: As a cell gets larger, its surface area to volume ratio:
questions.explain: Volume grows faster than surface area, constraining cell size.

questions.q: A structure found in plant cells but not typical animal cells is the:
questions.explain: Plant cells also often have chloroplasts and a large vacuole.

questions.q: The resolution of a microscope is its ability to:
options: Distinguish two close points as separate
questions.explain: Resolution concerns detail; magnification only enlarges the image.

questions.q: If an image is 40 mm wide at ×400 magnification, the actual width is:
questions.explain: Actual = 40 mm ÷ 400 = 0.1 mm = 100 µm.

questions.q: Complementary base pairing gives the DNA helix a constant width because:
options: A purine always pairs with a pyrimidine
questions.explain: Pairing a double-ring base with a single-ring base keeps the diameter uniform.
